standard.reference: 5520A Service Manual, Chapter 1 Specifications, printed pp. 1-6 to 1-25 (PDF pp. 22-41)
standard.author: typed from the page images by specs/build_5520a_standard.py

notes.1: SOURCE: Fluke 5520A Service Manual (supplied PDF 5520A_Manual.pdf), Chapter 1 Specifications, printed pp. 1-6 to 1-25 = PDF pp. 22-41 (printed 1-N = PDF N + 16). Rows carry the PDF page. Every value was read from rendered page images (130 dpi page, then a 200 dpi crop read a second time), not from extracted text.
notes.2: CONFIDENCE LEVEL: "Specification Confidence Interval 99 %" (General Specifications, printed p. 1-7, PDF p. 23). The sheet stores confidence_pct 99, so the coverage divisor is 2.576 (specmanager.divisor). Harmonised 2026-10-22 (the lab reports at 95 %, k = 2): the 5522A sheet is now also stored at 99 % (its Operators Manual p. 1-8 prints 99 %), the 5560A sheet is stored at its printed 95 % column (divisor 2). See NOTES.md, "Confidence level rule". To budget the 5520A with divisor 2 instead, set it in Standards Specs (logged).
notes.3: CONDITIONS (printed pp. 1-6, 1-7): valid after a 30 minute warm-up (or twice the time off); tcal = ambient temperature at calibration, tcal 15 to 35 degC; the tables hold for tcal +/-5 degC; outside it add 0.1 x (90 day or 1 year specification) per degC; zero cal every 7 days or when the ambient changes by more than 5 degC; the tightest ohms specification needs an ohms zero cal every 12 hours within +/-1 degC. The absolute uncertainty includes stability, temperature coefficient, linearity, line and load regulation and the traceability of the standards used for calibration: nothing is to be added for the temperature range indicated. EMC (p. 1-7): in fields of 1 to 3 V/m resistance outputs have a floor adder of 0.508 ohm (the unit glyph after 0.508 was not legible on the page image; read as ohm); not specified above 3 V/m; TC simulate / measure not specified above 0.4 V/m (pp. 1-8, 1-17).
notes.4: PERIODS: 90 day and 1 yr are both stored for every function the manual prints two columns for. Frequency (p. 1-23) prints ONE column, "1-Year Absolute Uncertainty": stored under 1 yr only (there is no 90 day value; none was invented). The 24 hour stability column (DC voltage, p. 1-8), noise and distortion columns, max burden and the compliance adders are not stored.
notes.5: RESOLUTION: taken from the manual's own resolution columns (res_src "manual"): DC voltage 0.1 uV .. 1000 uV (p. 1-8), DC current (p. 1-9), resistance 0.0001 .. 10000 ohm (p. 1-11), AC voltage 1 uV .. 10 mV (pp. 1-12, 1-13), AC current resolution table (p. 1-15, applies to LCOMP off and on), capacitance 0.1 pF .. 10 uF (p. 1-16), thermocouple 0.01 degC (p. 1-17 note [2]), RTD 0.003 degC (p. 1-18 note [1]), frequency 0.01 Hz .. 1 kHz (p. 1-23).
notes.6: RESISTANCE FLOOR: the table prints two floors, "12 hrs +/-1 degC" and "7 days +/-5 degC" since the ohms zero cal. Function "Resistance" holds the 12 hour floor (the tightest, the same choice the 5522A sheet makes: 0.001 ohm on the 0 to 11 ohm range). Function "Resistance [7 Day Zero Cal Floor]" holds the same ppm with the 7 day floor; it is excluded from a plain lookup and used only with variant="7 day". Footnote [2] (p. 1-11): the floors apply to 4-WIRE compensation only; for 2-WIRE and 2-WIRE COMP add 5 uV per amp of stimulus current to the floor (example 0.002 + 5 uV / 1 mA = 0.007 ohm): NOT included here (the stimulus current is not known to the budget), so a 2-wire budget is understated by that term. Footnote [3]: for currents below the allowable range the floor grows by Imin / Iactual: NOT applied.
notes.7: RANGE EDGES: the manual prints DC voltage and DC current ranges as "0 to X". They are stored as non-overlapping bands (the smallest range that holds the value, the rule specmanager.lookup uses for the other sheets): the printed text is kept in each row's "printed" field. DC voltage prints "30 V to 329.9999 V" and "100 V to 1000.000 V"; these overlap the 33 V and 330 V ranges and are stored as 33 V to 329.9999 V and 330 V to 1000 V (interpretation, NOT verified on the instrument; storing the printed 30 V / 100 V edges instead makes a lookup take the larger of the two overlapping rows). DC voltage 1000 to 1020 V is not covered by a printed row (the limits table p. 1-20 gives 0 to +/-1020 V; the AC table prints 330 V to 1020 V): a DC point above 1000 V finds no row.
notes.8: AUXILIARY output (dual output mode): DC voltage (p. 1-8) and AC voltage sine (p. 1-13) are stored in their own functions ("Auxiliary Output (Dual Output Mode)"), which a plain DCV / ACV lookup excludes. AUX AC is printed in % of output + uV (the NORMAL table is ppm of output + uV).
notes.9: PRINTED ANOMALIES (stored as read, flagged in problems): (a) DC current p. 1-9 first row is printed "0 to 329.999 mA" with resolution "1 nA"; the noise table below it says 329.999 uA, so it is stored as microamps; the resolution column of that table is printed in mA for rows 2 to 8 ("0.01 mA" ... "100 mA") but the digits of the ranges make them uA (3.29999 mA range: 0.01 uA), stored as uA-based values (10 nA ... 100 uA). (b) AC current LCOMP off, 3 A to 10.9999 A (p. 1-14) prints the second band "100 kHz to 1 kHz": stored as 100 Hz to 1 kHz (the next band is 1 kHz to 5 kHz, and the 11 A row prints 100 Hz to 1 kHz). (c) AC current LCOMP on, 3 A to 20.5 A footnote [3] (p. 1-15): "floor 1000 uA within 30 seconds, 5000 uA for operating times > 30 seconds" while the table prints 5000 uA (footnote [2] gives 4000 / 2000 for the lower band): the table value is stored; the footnote wording looks transposed. (d) Capacitance p. 1-16 prints "0.33 uF to 1.09999mF" for the 0.33 mF range: stored as 0.33 mF to 1.09999 mF. (e) The Pt 385 100 ohm RTD is NOT in the 5520A RTD table (p. 1-18: Pt 395, Pt 3926, Pt 3916 at 100 ohm; Pt 385 at 200, 500, 1000 ohm; PtNi 385 120 ohm; Cu 427 10 ohm), unlike the 5522A sheet. (f) The general specifications table (p. 1-7) says "5500A Calibrator" for weight / power / dimensions (a manual-wide wording quirk); the 5520A is the instrument of every table.
notes.10: TEMPERATURE: thermocouple types B C E J K L N R S T U, 90 day and 1 yr, in degC; the manual prints one "Source/Measure" column, stored for both directions (functions "... Output" = the calibrator sources, "... Input" = it measures). Resolution 0.01 degC; standard ITS-90 or IPTS-68 selectable; note [3]: does not include thermocouple error. The manual prints no reference-junction condition beyond tcal +/-5 degC (p. 1-17). Type K values are identical to the 5522A sheet. RTD (p. 1-18): COMP OFF (NORMAL terminals) and 2-wire / 4-wire compensation, resolution 0.003 degC; Cu 427 is based on MINCO Application Aid No. 18.
notes.11: NOT STORED: DC power and AC power (pp. 1-18, 1-19 summaries in % of watts output), power / dual-output limits (summarised in "limits"), phase (p. 1-21), harmonics (p. 1-25), AC voltage and current non-sine and extended bandwidth (pp. 1-25 .. 1-30, summarised in "limits"), AC voltage DC offset, TC linear 10 uV/degC and 1 mV/degC modes (p. 1-8: 50 ppm + 3 uV 1 yr), and the SC300 / SC600 scope-option specifications (chapters 6 and 7). The 5522A sheet carries the scope-option rows; this one does not, so scope bandwidth / time base points cannot be costed on it.

limits.limit: 330 V to 1020 V: 45 Hz to 10 kHz only (45 Hz-1 kHz, 1-5 kHz, 5-10 kHz); 33 V to 329.999 V: 45 Hz to 100 kHz; 3.3 V to 32.9999 V: 10 Hz to 100 kHz; below 3.3 V: 10 Hz to 500 kHz. Maximum specified frequency 500 kHz.

Typical / wide specification only (5 % of output + 0.5 % of range): 0.01 Hz to 9.99 Hz on all NORMAL ranges to 33 V; 0.3 V to 3.3 V from 500.1 kHz to 1 MHz (-10 dB at 1 MHz, typical) and 1.001 MHz to 2 MHz (-31 dB at 2 MHz, typical); AUX 0.01 Hz to 9.99 Hz.
10 mV to 5 V, 10 Hz to 30 kHz; the 3.3 V to 5 V range only to 10 kHz; the maximum frequency of the dual output is 30 kHz.
29 uA to 329.99 mA: 10 Hz to 30 kHz; 0.33 A to 2.99999 A: 10 Hz to 10 kHz; 3 A to 20.5 A: 45 Hz to 5 kHz (nothing below 45 Hz).
29 uA to 329.99 mA: 10 Hz to 1 kHz; 0.33 A to 2.99999 A: 10 Hz to 440 Hz; 3 A to 20.5 A: 10 Hz to 1 kHz. Compliance limits 7 / 7 / 5 / 5 / 4 / 3 V rms by range (p. 1-15).

DC and AC: continuous below 11 A; above 11 A the time allowed is 60 - T - I minutes in any 60 minutes (T = ambient degC, I = amps), Figure 1-4 (p. 1-10); floor is larger within 30 s of selecting operate (DC 1500 uA then 750 uA; AC LCOMP on 4000 / 2000 uA).
Voltage 0 to +/-1020 V; current 0 to +/-20.5 A; AUX voltage 0 to +/-7 V; AC AUX 10 mV to 5 V.

45 Hz to 65 Hz: 33 mV to 1000 V with 3.3 mA to 20.5 A; 65 Hz to 500 Hz: 330 mV to 1000 V (33 mA to 2.99999 A) or 3.3 V to 1000 V (33 mA to 20.5 A); 500 Hz to 1 kHz: 330 mV to 1000 V, 33 mA to 20.5 A; 1 kHz to 5 kHz: 3.3 V to 1000 V (limited to 500 V in dual voltage mode), 33 mA to 2.99999 A; 5 kHz to 10 kHz: 3.3 V to 1000 V (250 V in dual voltage mode), 33 mA to 329.99 mA. Phase 0 to +/-179.99 deg, resolution 0.01 deg.

0.19 nF to 110 mF continuously variable; maximum peak voltage 3 V; maximum peak current 150 mA, rms 30 mA below 1.1 uF and 100 mA from 1.1 uF; lead resistance 10 ohm maximum in 2-wire COMP; allowed frequency / charge-discharge rate by range (10 Hz to 10 kHz on the smallest ranges down to 0 to 0.2 Hz on 110 mF).
Continuously variable 0 ohm to 1.1 Gohm; allowable current by range from 1 mA to 125 mA (0 to 33 ohm) down to 1 nA to 13 nA (330 Mohm to 1100 Mohm).
0.01 Hz to 2.000 MHz; jitter 100 ns; 2.5 ppm +/-5 uHz (internal reference, 1 year); with REF CLK external: the uncertainty of the external 10 MHz clock +/-5 uHz (1 V to 5 V p-p).

problems.what: Typed from the 5520A Service Manual specification tables (printed pp. 1-7 to 1-23); no approval signature. Confidence level 99 % is printed (p. 1-7) and stored; divisor 2.576. The 5522A sheet states none (divisor 2) and the 5560A sheet is 95 % (divisor 2): the three calibrators are not on one confidence basis (NOTES.md).
The manual prints "30 V to 329.9999 V" and "100 V to 1000.000 V". Stored as 33 V to 329.9999 V and 330 V to 1000 V (the instrument ranges); see note 7. Interpretation, not verified.
No printed DC voltage row above 1000 V although the output limit is 1020 V (p. 1-20).
Printed "0 to 329.999 mA" (p. 1-9) but the noise table and the 1 nA resolution make it 329.999 uA; stored as microamps.
The printed resolution column carries the unit "mA" on every row below the first (0.01 mA ... 100 mA); the digits of the range make them uA. Stored as 10 nA ... 100 uA.
Second band printed "100 kHz to 1 kHz" (p. 1-14); stored as 100 Hz to 1 kHz.
Footnote [3] (p. 1-15) words the floor within / after 30 seconds the other way round to the table; the table value (5000 uA) is stored.
Printed "0.33 uF to 1.09999mF" (p. 1-16); stored as 0.33 mF to 1.09999 mF.
No Pt 385 100 ohm row in the 5520A table (p. 1-18); the 5522A sheet has one. A lookup for that RTD finds nothing.
Floors are the 4-wire values (footnote [2], p. 1-11). 2-wire / 2-wire COMP add 5 uV per amp of stimulus current: not included.
The manual prints a 1 year column only; there is no 90 day specification for frequency.
Not stored: stability, noise, burden, compliance adders, power, phase, harmonics, non-sine and extended bandwidth AC, TC linear modes, SC300 / SC600 (note 11).
